models_evaluated: Batch-Constrained deep Q-learning (semi-Markov) warfarin dosing model

links.outcome: Compared RL warfarin dosing model against rules-based algorithm for TTR and composite clinical outcome
links.effect: RL: each 10% increase in algorithm-consistent dosing gave 6.78% TTR improvement and HR 0.89; rules-based benchmark gave 6.10% TTR improvement and HR 0.90, so results were comparable.
links.quote: These results were comparable to those of a rules-based clinical algorithm used for benchmarking, for which each 10% increase in algorithm-consistent dosing independently predicted a 6.10% increase in TTR (95% CI 5.67, 6.54, p < 0.001) and a 10% decrease in the composite outcome (HR 0.90; 95% CI 0.83, 0.98, p = 0.018).

screen.reason: The study develops and externally validates a deep reinforcement learning model for warfarin dosing using retrospective clinical trial datasets, without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
